Mutable array references

Source: R/refs.R
refs.Rd

Ports of jax.new_ref, jax.empty_ref, jax.free_ref, jax.freeze, jax.Ref and jax.ds. new_ref(x) makes a reference holding the array x; read it with r[...] (NumPy indexing, r[] for the whole value) or r$get(), and write it with r[...] <- value, r$set(value, ...) or r$addupdate(value, ...). freeze(r) returns the value and makes the reference read only; free_ref(r) releases it. ds() builds a dynamic slice index ds(start, size, stride) for reference indexing.

Usage

new_ref(init_val, memory_space = NULL, kind = NULL)

empty_ref(ty, memory_space = NULL, pin = FALSE)

free_ref(ref)

freeze(ref)

Ref(...)

ds(start, size, stride = 1L)

Arguments

init_val

Initial value.

memory_space, kind, pin

Accepted for compatibility.

ty

A ShapeDtypeStruct() for empty_ref (the value starts as zeros).

ref

A reference.

...

Ignored: Ref names the class of references (port of jax.Ref) and cannot be called to build one.

start, size, stride

Start (static or traced), static size and stride of ds().

Value

new_ref() and empty_ref() return a reference (class jax_ref); freeze() returns an array; free_ref() returns NULL invisibly; ds() returns an index.

Details

Refs may be read and written inside jit(), grad() and vmap(): refs created inside the transformed function behave as in JAX. jit() also handles refs passed as arguments or closed over (their updates become outputs written back after each call). vmap() maps a ref passed as an argument through its value: the function sees a ref holding one element, and the ref holds the stacked result afterwards. A ref that the body of lax_scan(), lax_while_loop(), lax_fori_loop() or a branch of lax_cond() closes over is state of that operation. In other cases, writing an outer ref inside a transformation leaves it holding a traced value that is unusable outside, as JAX forbids.
